title: Asterion authored region material sources
mode: Built-in image_gen tool; original inner material generation plus referenced-image geographic/weather extension edits
purpose: Surface-only geography and a separate cloud-density material on real spherical geometry. No screenshot scenery.

terrain.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: ORIGINAL surface albedo material texture for a real 3D spherical planet in a premium orbital racing game. This is a flat material map only, NOT an illustration of a planet or game scene.
Create a photorealistic cloud-free nadir satellite mosaic of a coherent fictional coastal mountain region. Output landscape 3072 x 2048, edge-to-edge terrain and ocean. Orthographic directly downward projection, uniform scale, absolutely no perspective, horizon, globe, sky, buildings, roads, spacecraft, labels or text.
Composition: the left 55% contains a large tectonically formed continent, the right 45% contains deep navy ocean. The continent has a sharply articulated east-facing coast: one long tapering peninsula aimed toward the lower-right, a deep hooked bay near the upper-center, a chain of small offshore volcanic islands. A long sinuous folded mountain range runs north-south well inland, with branching ridges, narrow pale rock summits and deeply incised valleys. Several distinct dendritic river basins descend from those mountains into green coastal lowlands, two braided estuaries and natural sediment fans. Windward slopes are subdued deep olive forest, lee-side plateaus muted ochre and brown, high terrain grey bare rock with only sparse tiny snowfields on the highest summit. Biomes follow elevation, drainage and rain shadow; no uniform random mottling. Ocean shows a narrow subdued turquoise continental shelf tracing the real coast, estuarine suspended sediment, then dark open water with subtle large-scale current variation.
Material requirements: exceptional fine natural topographic detail at satellite scale, coherent geography from macro structure to tiny tributaries; restrained natural colors. Neutral diffuse white illumination, minimal directional shadows, no baked sunset/glints or dramatic photographic contrast. Absolutely NO clouds, haze, atmosphere or fog; those will be rendered on a separate mesh in real time. No artificial texture/noise blotches, no painterly strokes, no map symbols or border. Ocean continues to the full right, top-right and lower-right edges. Mainland continues naturally through left edge.

clouds.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: original GRAYSCALE optical-density material map for a separate cloud sphere above a 3D planet. This is a flat technical raster texture, not a finished scene.
Create a photorealistic satellite-nadir CLOUD-ONLY map. Landscape 3:2 ratio, finest possible native detail. Pure black represents clear air, opaque white represents dense cloud top, continuous greys represent thin cloud. Edge-to-edge uniform orthographic scale, exactly straight down. NO earth, land, water, coastlines, horizon, stars, sky, atmosphere, labels or color whatsoever.
Design a coherent regional weather composition: about 65% clear black negative space, especially through the center and center-left. A large organized curled storm lies near the upper-right edge, partly outside the frame; its dense curved head has layered billowing structure, opening into fine feathered cirrus outflow and a broken trailing front sweeping toward the lower-right. One much smaller group of low stratocumulus sits near the lower-left corner; around it are several sparse irregular cloud streets with varied cell sizes. Cloud types and scales must be distinct: kilometres-wide organized weather, mesoscopic billow clusters, sharply resolved tiny cotton-like convective turrets, delicate thin fibrous cirrus. Avoid a uniform speckle/noise field, repeated evenly sized islands, generic Perlin noise, horizontal smear bands, hard-edged graphic swirls, painterly curls.
Illumination requirement: treat this as density data. White and grey reflect cloud thickness only; do not bake a directional sun or cast shadows into this map. Crisp natural structure with soft physical optical edges. No border, text or watermark.

processing: Selected native PNGs copied without pixel edits. The original inner texture UVs and blend weight remain unchanged. Surrounding terrain is registered with a smooth bounded coordinate transform; extra latitude coverage keeps ridge/coast structure continuous into the visible cap, while surrounding organized weather replaces the procedural far-cloud field. No upsampling or new noise. Surface water response comes from chromatic separation; cloud density is remapped in shader into coverage and top-height channels. Procedural whole-sphere maps remain only outside the authored visible cap. Two rejected terrain extent attempts are not project assets or runtime loads. No external source assets, licensing dependencies, or API key.

surroundingTerrain.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Input image1 is the edit target: cloudfree satellite albedo of a fictional coastal mountain region. OUTPUT A TALL PORTRAIT IMAGE, 2:3 width:height, 1024x1536 or larger. The entire wide landscape input is preserved as a small horizontal band THROUGH THE MIDDLE of this portrait output, occupying center67% of width and center30% of height (x16.5%-83.5%, y35%-65%). The new canvas extends mainly NORTH AND SOUTH: add vast new geography above and below the original, with smaller extensions at left and right. The original top and bottom are now far from the output top and bottom! Do not output a landscape image. Do not stretch the original to fillportrait. Keep original coastal landmarks at the same shape in the center band.
Outpaint a coherent continuation of its mountain belt, continental west and maritime east. Match all natural tiny terrain details and muted colors, keep ridge and river frequency consistent throughout north/south additions. Above the original region, the mountain range bends northwest and branches into parallel smaller folded ranges, the coastal line bends northwest too and includes a deep natural gulf. Below original region, the mountain chain continues southeast into a dry rocky tapering peninsula with complex bays; broad deep navy sea continues east through all the right side. West is ochre arid plateaus with green branching river valleys and mountain rain shadows, east-facing mountain slopes subdued olive-green forest. Coasts have finely serrated headlands, narrow turquoise shelves, estuaries, tiny offshore islands. No broad smooth beige landblobs. Original small tributaries/ridges remain small and crisply resolved in new area, no uniform mottling. Entireoutput is uniformorthographic satellite nadir with no perspective; original region and newlyauthored geography share same physical feature scale.
This is a technical flat ALBEDO MATERIAL MAP for real spherical geometry, NOT an illustrated globe. NO clouds, haze, fog, atmosphere, horizon, sphere, stars, spacecraft, buildings, roads, text, symbols, borders. Diffuse neutral daylight, minimal baked shading, no directional illumination or glints. Preserve input exact dark navy ocean, muted green/ochre/grey terrain color family. New geography goes to ALL edges of tallportrait output.

surroundingClouds.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Input image1 is the edit target, a technical GRAYSCALE satellite cloud optical-density map. Expand the geographic coverage greatly. Place the entire input in the central ONE THIRD of width and ONE THIRD of height, preserving the original storm and black clear center at that reduced relative size, and OUTPAINT new connected weather into ALL the surrounding area. Output landscape3:2. Strictly orthographic nadir, uniform map scale, tiny crisp meteorological detail across the entire canvas. This is cloud-density data: black=clear air, white=dense cloud top, grey=thin cloud, no lighting shadows.
Continue the original storm near inputupperright into its complete organized cyclonic system, with delicate feathered outflow spreading northeast and curved broken frontal bands moving southwest. New outer areas have broad contiguous black clear sectors separating synoptic-scale fronts; overall65-70% black clearair. Add only one secondary smaller broken front toward the farleft edge with finer stratocumulus streets, and one sparse isolated patch farnorth. No uniformly scattered cloudblobs. Variedscale from broad coherent synoptic fronts to finelyresolved cotton turrets, fragile cirrus fibers and grouped cloudstreets. Avoid giant smooth white masses, grayscale noise fields, stipple everywhere or regularly repeated little islands. Keep the central original clear corridor and original storm composition. All edge areas must be just as materially detailed as the center. No rectangular patch seams.
NO terrain, water, oceans, coastlines, stars, horizon, sphere silhouette, atmosphere, perspective, planet image, color, text, mapsymbols or border. Flat continuous grayscale density texture only. Highest native resolution available, ideally3072x2048.
